description: How drugs work, drug categories, pharmacokinetics, and medication safety

pharmacokinetics.definition: What the body does to a drug (ADME)
pharmacokinetics.absorption: How drug enters bloodstream; route affects speed and completeness
pharmacokinetics.distribution: How drug spreads through body; depends on blood flow, protein binding, lipid solubility
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Transformation of drug (primarily liver); cytochrome P450 enzymes
pharmacokinetics.excretion: Elimination (primarily kidneys); half-life determines dosing frequency
pharmacokinetics.half_life: Time for drug concentration to fall by 50%; 4–5 half-lives to reach steady state

pharmacodynamics.definition: What the drug does to the body
pharmacodynamics.receptor: Protein target that drug binds to; most drugs work through receptors
pharmacodynamics.agonist: Binds receptor and activates it; mimics natural ligand
pharmacodynamics.antagonist: Binds receptor but doesn't activate; blocks natural ligand
pharmacodynamics.partial_agonist: Activates receptor but with lower maximal effect
pharmacodynamics.dose_response: Higher dose = greater effect up to a maximum

drug_routes.oral_po: Swallowed; convenient; first-pass metabolism reduces bioavailability
drug_routes.intravenous_iv: Into vein; 100% bioavailability; fastest onset; irreversible
drug_routes.intramuscular_im: Into muscle; faster than oral; slower than IV
drug_routes.subcutaneous_sc: Under skin; depot for slow release (e.g., insulin)
drug_routes.sublingual: Under tongue; bypasses first-pass; fast onset (e.g., nitroglycerin)
drug_routes.inhalation: Through lungs; fast onset; localized for respiratory drugs
drug_routes.transdermal: Through skin patch; slow sustained delivery (e.g., fentanyl, nicotine)

antibiotics.resistance: Major global health threat; overuse drives resistance

analgesics.nsaids: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory; block COX enzymes; ibuprofen, aspirin, naproxen
analgesics.acetaminophen: Paracetamol; pain and fever; mechanism not fully understood; no anti-inflammatory
analgesics.opioids: Bind opioid receptors; powerful pain relief; high addiction risk; morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl

cardiovascular.statins: Lower LDL cholesterol; inhibit HMG-CoA reductase; atorvastatin, simvastatin
cardiovascular.ace_inhibitors: Block angiotensin converting enzyme; lower blood pressure; enalapril, lisinopril
cardiovascular.beta_blockers: Block beta-adrenergic receptors; slow heart rate; metoprolol, atenolol
cardiovascular.diuretics: Increase urine output; lower blood pressure; furosemide (loop), hydrochlorothiazide (thiazide)

psychotropics.ssri: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors; depression/anxiety; fluoxetine, sertraline, citalopram
psychotropics.snri: Also inhibit norepinephrine reuptake; venlafaxine, duloxetine
psychotropics.antipsychotics: Block dopamine/serotonin receptors; schizophrenia, bipolar; risperidone, olanzapine
psychotropics.benzodiazepines: GABA agonists; anxiety, sedation; diazepam, lorazepam; dependency risk

drug_interactions.pharmacokinetic: Drug A changes absorption/metabolism/excretion of Drug B
drug_interactions.pharmacodynamic: Drugs have additive, synergistic, or antagonistic effects

common_examples.statins_grapefruit: Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4; increases statin levels and toxicity
common_examples.maois_tyramine: Hypertensive crisis with aged cheeses, wines

medication_safety.polypharmacy: Use of 5+ medications; increases interaction risk; especially in elderly
medication_safety.off_label: Prescribing for unapproved indication; legal and common
medication_safety.generic_vs_brand: Same active ingredient; bioequivalent; typically 80–85% cheaper
